evals.prompt: Our app has 50,000 downloads but only 800 daily actives. We're buying more installs.
evals.expected_output: Should stop the install buying. D1/D7/D30 retention has not flattened, so acquisition is filling a bucket with no bottom. Should note consumer churn of 5-10% monthly is common and retention IS the product because there is no contractual inertia. Should require the retention curve flatten before spending, and ask what the return trigger is.
assertions: Explains the retention curve must flatten first
Cites consumer churn benchmarks of 5-10% monthly
States retention is the product for consumer
Makes the return trigger explicit: names what would bring users back tomorrow

evals.prompt: How do we make our fitness app go viral?
evals.expected_output: Should design the shareable artifact rather than a referral program. Should cite Wordle going from 90 to 2,000,000 players on a spoiler-free emoji grid and extract the principles: encodes the result without spoiling, socially safe to post, plain text that travels anywhere, no ask. Should design for what makes the sharer look good and consider a fixed daily or annual moment.
assertions: Focuses on a shareable artifact over a referral program
Cites Wordle and its growth numbers
Names socially-safe sharing as the constraint
States designing for the sharer, not the company
Warns against a share button that broadcasts an ad
Considers a recurring moment like Wrapped or a streak
